title: Diagnostic accuracy of a command centre boarding-risk flag against observed emergency department boarding
subtitle: Accuracy, calibration and spectrum of a deployed flag, with boarding of four hours or more as the reference standard
statement: A patient flow command centre flags admitted emergency patients whose boarding-risk score exceeds a vendor threshold, so that bed managers can escalate them. The score has never been checked locally, median boarding is still 5.1 hours, and clinicians suspect the flag marks obvious cases and misses others. The hospital needs to know the flag's sensitivity and specificity for boarding of four hours or more, the score's calibration, and whether accuracy differs by time of day, weekday and admitting service.
whoAffected: Admitted emergency patients who wait for beds, emergency and inpatient clinicians, bed managers and command centre staff.
whatHurts: Prolonged boarding is associated with worse care and crowding; if the flag misses patients who will board, escalation goes to the wrong patients and the command centre's effort is wasted.
currentPractice: A vendor score computed at the admission decision, a fixed flag threshold on the wall display, and escalation by bed managers; no local validation.
whyNow: Eighteen months of logged scores, a data governance approval and persistent boarding despite the command centre.
constraints: No research funding; the score cannot be changed or retrained during the evaluation; the command centre analyst is available one day a week until June 2027; data come only from existing timestamps and the score log.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients at highest risk of long waits for a bed are identified early enough for escalation to shorten their wait.
summary: Problem framed as a diagnostic accuracy study of a deployed boarding-risk flag.
